summary: Intermittent 429s for mixed SSE + gRPC streams after subaccount reparent in Private VPC
description:
Issue summary:
Customer DataFerry reports intermittent 429 responses for a subset of long-lived SSE subscribers and concurrent gRPC ingestion streams after they performed a subaccount reparent operation (moved streaming workload from subaccount A -> B) in their Private VPC deployment. Impact: multiple production ingestion workers and real-time dashboards were rate-limited causing data lag and backlog.

Impact:
- ~12% of SSE connections observed 429s over a 2 hour window during nightly export; gRPC clients report sporadic rejections for otherwise identical requests.
- Business impact: delayed analytics pipelines, elevated error rates on dashboards, escalated by on-call.

Environment:
- Deployment: Private (customer-managed VPC) behind their NAT gateway + customer edge LB -> Redwood edge-proxy (v2.4.1).
- Region: prod-us-west.
- Relevant components: ingress-proxy, edge token windowing rate-limiter, route-weighting for streaming lanes, subaccount reparent event executed at 02:10 UTC.

Steps to reproduce (as performed by customer):
1) Start mixed workload: 300 SSE subscribers to /events and 60 concurrent gRPC streaming workers to /v1/streams using the same top-level API key but different subaccount-scoped keys.
2) Trigger subaccount reparent via Console API (move workload from subaccount A to B).
3) Observe connection churn as clients re-auth; ~30% of clients reconnect within 90s due to orchestration.
4) Customer sees a wave of 429s affecting ~40% of reconnecting SSEs and a smaller subset of gRPC calls.

Observed behavior:
- Rate-limiter records show the same physical API token being charged twice across two different route fingerprints for a short epoch, then a sudden token-window depletion and subsequent 429 rejects.
- Edge-proxy logs contain many reconnects with changing TLS session fingerprints and repeated preflight probes from health-check sidecars.
- Customer's NAT gateway has limited ephemeral ports and exhibits high NAT churn at the time of the reparent.

Expected behavior:
- Reparent/migration should not double-count tokens or cause persistent 429 waves for reconnecting clients; reconnects should be accounted idempotently or allowed a short grace window for migrating sessions.

Samples / logs provided by customer (sanitized):
- Edge-proxy snippets showing token_id=ak_*** charged at 02:11:17 and again at 02:11:19 with different connection_fingerprint values.
- Rate-limiter debug: refill_epoch=1617 drifted on 2 of 3 nodes; duplicate_count spikes coincide with NAT port churn.
- Client-side traces: SSE reconnects show 100-300ms jitter, health-check probes every 10s during reconnect window.

Additional notes:
- Customer had a background bulk-export that increased preflight traffic during the same window.
- They are on a private deployment with some ingress controls (their load balancer terminates TLS, rewrites headers).
comments: 2026-03-10 10:45 - Aisha Patel (Support): Case opened after DataFerry flagged production 429s affecting ingestion. Collected initial logs, asked customer to capture edge-proxy debug logs and rate-limiter snapshots.
2026-03-10 13:02 - Customer (DataFerry): Provided sanitized edge-proxy logs and NAT utilization graph. Confirmed subaccount reparent occurred at 02:10 UTC.

2026-03-11 09:18 - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Preliminary triage - seeing duplicate token accounting on two edge nodes around the reparent window. Suspect fingerprinting + NAT port churn causing split accounting. Requested rate-limiter histograms and token ledger for the period.

2026-03-11 16:03 - Eng (Rate-limiter): Found refill_epoch drift on one rate-limiter replica (node rl-3). Replica was slow to apply epoch commit, causing a brief window where the same token was allowed on two nodes. Correlated with high reconnect rate.

2026-03-12 08:22 - Customer: Confirmed they had a sidecar health-check that aggressively probed reconnecting clients. They agreed to temporarily disable health-checks for the SSE service during migration.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: NAT port churn + edge TLS session changes lead to different connection fingerprints for the same API key; fingerprinting logic caused duplicate accounting across two route-buckets.

Hypothesis 2: One rate-limiter replica (rl-3) had epoch commit delay (observed GC pause) which, combined with reconnect burst, resulted in transient double-count of token until leader commit reconciled.

Evidence: rate-limiter logs show duplicate charge events with identical token_id and separate connection_fingerprint values within the same refill epoch window. NAT gateway metrics show ephemeral port exhaustion events at the same timestamps.
Action taken: pulled rate-limiter token ledger for rl-1/rl-2/rl-3, edge-proxy reconnect traces, and customer's NAT port usage charts.
Reproduction attempts in staging: triggered coordinated reconnects + short epoch commit introduced artificially on one replica; reproduced duplicate charge pattern and transient 429 wave.
resolution: Short-term mitigation applied (2026-03-12): Redwood support granted a temporary quota bump for DataFerry for 6 hours and disabled aggressive preflight counting for SSE routes in the ingress-proxy for this tenant. Customer disabled health-check sidecar during their reparent operations per our suggestion.

Medium-term fix planned: rate-limiter patch to dedupe token charges across connection fingerprints within the same refill epoch and to add a configurable grace window for subaccount reparent operations (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter/pull/140).

Customer recommendations provided: increase NAT ephemeral port pool on their LB, avoid aggressive health-check probes during large reconnect waves, and configure isolated burst pool for long-lived SSEs vs bulk-export workers.

Monitoring/follow-up: created alert rule to detect refill_epoch drift and a dashboard for per-tenant duplicate-charge counts. Follow-up owner: Marco Ruiz. Postmortem scheduled and linked to INC-2026-331.
Status: keeping ticket open until rate-limiter patch deploys to Private VPCs and customer's configuration changes are validated in their next migration window.
